name: GHS Urban Centre Database 2025 (R2024A), general characteristics

measures.definition: Straight-line distance from the city's centre point to the nearest edge of its urban centre outline (touching 1 km squares with at least 1,500 residents per km², 50,000 people or more, 2025), over directions that lead on to land.

rights.edition: GHS-UCDB R2024A V1.2, general characteristics theme (2026-05-19)
rights.attribution: GHS-UCDB R2024A, European Commission, Joint Research Centre, CC BY 4.0, doi:10.2905/1a338be6-7eaf-480c-9664-3a8ade88cbcd; Borgo derives the distance from the centre to the urban centre's edge
notices: Shores and lakes from Natural Earth (public domain) decide which directions lead on to land.

vetted.notes: Credit: Mari Rivero et al. (2024), GHS-UCDB R2024A, European Commission JRC, doi:10.2905/1a338be6-7eaf-480c-9664-3a8ade88cbcd. Sea and lakes from Natural Earth (public domain) decide which directions lead on to land.

caveats: The urban centre ends where density falls below 1,500 residents per km²: beyond it lie suburbs, farmland, hills or a large park, not necessarily open country.
Shores come from Natural Earth at about 1 km precision; directions that meet water within 3 km of the edge are dropped.
A centre point that falls in a gap inside its urban centre gets no figure (Dubai).
